criteria_results.title: IP section revised from ownership to perpetual-license construct
criteria_results.reasoning: Although the operative Section 5.2 adopts Vendor ownership with an irrevocable, perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free license to Customer, Draft 3 also inserts an alternative stating that Customer ownership remains reserved for further negotiation. That continues to demand/preserve the ownership position despite TechNova’s acceptance of the perpetual-license construct.

criteria_results.title: Non-assertion covenant included in IP section
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 includes a broad Vendor non-assertion covenant in Section 5.2 covering Customer’s worldwide access, use, reproduction, modification, deployment, maintenance, and further development of the Customer-Trained Adaptations, including fine-tuned adapter weights, and it expressly applies after expiration or termination.

criteria_results.title: API-based weight export portability within 30 days in industry-standard format
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly requires Vendor to provide an API-based export of all Customer-Trained Adaptations, including fine-tuned adapter weights, within 30 days after termination or expiration, in an industry-standard, machine-readable format such as ONNX or SafeTensors. The Initial SOW also repeats this portability requirement.

criteria_results.title: Escrow provisions included as part of IP protective measures
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 includes a dedicated Article 5A technology escrow framework tied to the perpetual-license construct in Section 5.2. It requires deposit of fine-tuned adapter weights, training configuration files, and pipeline artifacts, with update, verification, release-trigger, post-release license, and cost provisions; Exhibit E further documents the escrow terms.

criteria_results.title: General liability cap at 1.5× annual fees ($3,600,000)
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 10.2 sets the general aggregate liability cap at 1.5× the $2,400,000 Annual Platform Fee, expressly equal to $3,600,000. The updated issues list also accurately reflects this amount.

criteria_results.title: Super-cap at 3× annual fees ($7,200,000) for IP indemnity and data-breach carve-outs
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 10.3 applies an aggregate super-cap of three times the $2,400,000 Annual Platform Fee—$7,200,000—to Vendor liability for Article 6 data-processing/data-breach matters and indemnification obligations under Sections 11.1 and 11.2, including IP indemnity.

criteria_results.title: Willful misconduct and gross negligence remain fully uncapped
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 10.3 expressly provides that liability arising from either party’s willful misconduct or gross negligence is not subject to the General Cap or consequential-damages exclusion and “shall remain fully uncapped.” The $7.2 million super-cap applies only to specified data/privacy and indemnification liabilities, not willful misconduct or gross negligence.

criteria_results.title: CCPA service-provider designation and certification
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly requires Vendor to act as a CCPA service provider and processor, not an independent controller. Section 6.2 references Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(ag) and requires certification in the DPA; Exhibit D likewise certifies Vendor's service-provider status under § 1798.140(ag).

criteria_results.title: Prohibition on use of Customer Data for model improvement with de-identification conditions
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 specifically prohibits use of Customer Data, including de-identified or aggregated derivatives, for model improvement unless the data satisfies Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(m) and an independent third-party assessor approved in writing by Customer verifies compliance before use. Sections 6.1 and DPA 5A state these as express contractual obligations.

criteria_results.title: Uptime SLA at 99.95% monthly
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly sets the Platform availability requirement at 99.95% for each calendar month in Section 9.1, and Exhibit B repeats the monthly Platform Uptime target as ≥ 99.95%.

criteria_results.title: Uptime SLA exclusions for scheduled maintenance and force majeure
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly excludes scheduled maintenance windows and Force Majeure Events from Downtime in Section 9.1. Exhibit B also preserves both exclusions and specifies the scheduled-maintenance conditions, including 72 hours’ notice and a four-hour monthly limit.

criteria_results.title: Latency SLA at p95 ≤ 450 ms in Draft 3
criteria_results.reasoning: Although Section 9.2 and Exhibit B Section 4A use p95 ≤ 450 ms, Exhibit B’s Service Levels table still states p95 ≤ 400 ms. Draft 3 therefore does not consistently set the latency SLA at 450 ms.

criteria_results.title: Issues list flags latency as yellow-zone item (450 ms vs. product team's 400 ms preference)
criteria_results.reasoning: The issues list identifies latency as “p95 ≤ 450 ms,” marks it as “YELLOW — product-critical caution,” and expressly notes that Priya/product team continues to prefer sub-400 ms for LendStream real-time decisioning.

criteria_results.title: F1 accuracy threshold at ≥ 0.92 initial
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 sets the initial Model Accuracy SLA at F1 ≥ 0.92 during the 90-day Stabilization Period, and the Initial SOW likewise requires a target accuracy of F1 ≥ 0.92.

criteria_results.title: F1 ramp mechanism to ≥ 0.94 after 90-day stabilization period post-Go-Live
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 contractually sets F1 ≥ 0.92 during the 90-day production stabilization period from October 1 through December 31, 2025, and ramps the target to F1 ≥ 0.94 beginning January 1, 2026, consistent with the required post-Go-Live mechanism.

criteria_results.title: SLA service credits capped at 20% of monthly fees ($40,000)
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly caps aggregate SLA Service Credits at 20% of the $200,000 monthly Annual Platform Fee installment, equal to $40,000 per month, in Section 9.4 and Exhibit B, Section 5(c).

criteria_results.title: Termination right for 3 consecutive months of SLA miss retained
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 retains the termination right in Section 9.5: if Vendor fails to meet any SLA target for three or more consecutive calendar months, Customer may terminate on 30 days’ written notice without an early termination fee. Section 13.5 and Exhibit B also preserve this trigger.

criteria_results.title: New AI-output indemnity provision inserted
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 inserts a new Section 11.2, “AI-Output Indemnification,” requiring Vendor to defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer against third-party claims alleging that AI-generated outputs infringe or misappropriate third-party intellectual property rights or violate applicable law.

criteria_results.title: AI-output indemnity carve-out for Customer modification or off-label use
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 11.2 expressly excludes indemnity to the extent a claim is caused by Customer’s modification of an output after receipt or Customer’s use of the output outside the documented use case in the applicable SOW.

criteria_results.title: IP indemnity scope broadened to all intellectual property rights
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 broadens Section 11.1 beyond registered U.S. patents and copyrights to cover all Intellectual Property Rights worldwide, expressly including patents, copyrights, trade secrets, trademarks, service marks, trade dress, moral rights, database rights, and analogous foreign rights arising from authorized use of the Platform, Base Model, Customer-Trained Adaptations, or outputs.

criteria_results.title: Escrow of adapter weights plus training configuration and pipeline artifacts
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 replaces the full Base Model source-code escrow requirement with escrow of all fine-tuned adapter weights, training configuration files, and pipeline artifacts necessary to use or deploy those weights. The agreement and Exhibit E consistently reflect this scope.

criteria_results.title: Iron Mountain IPM as proposed escrow agent with NCC Group as acceptable alternative
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 names Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Management, Inc. as the proposed escrow agent in the agreement and Exhibit E. The updated issues list also expressly identifies NCC Group plc as an acceptable alternative if Meridian objects to Iron Mountain.

criteria_results.title: Escrow release triggers include insolvency, material uncured breach (>60 days), and cessation of product support
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 includes all three required escrow release triggers in Section 5A.3: Vendor insolvency/bankruptcy, a material breach remaining uncured for more than 60 days after notice, and cessation or discontinuation of MeridianIQ Platform support.

criteria_results.title: Tech E&O insurance accepted at $5M per occurrence in Draft 3
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 sets Technology Errors & Omissions / Cyber Liability Insurance at $5,000,000 per occurrence in Section 12.1(b), accepting Meridian’s current policy limit.

criteria_results.title: Issues list flags Tech E&O as yellow-zone item (playbook prefers $10M for TCV > $5M)
criteria_results.reasoning: Issue 11 flags the accepted $5M Tech E&O coverage as a “YELLOW ZONE” because TCV exceeds $5M and states the fallback is to seek $10M per occurrence, satisfying the playbook preference for the $7.2M TCV.

criteria_results.title: Delaware governing law maintained in Draft 3
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 maintains Delaware governing law in Section 14.1, which states that the Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware. No other state's law is specified as governing law.

criteria_results.title: Delaware courts (Court of Chancery or U.S. District Court for D. Del.) as dispute forum
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 14.2 specifies exclusive dispute resolution in the Delaware Court of Chancery or, where subject-matter jurisdiction exists, the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware, and does not require arbitration.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes CCPA service-provider certification language
criteria_results.reasoning: Exhibit D, Section 3 expressly includes a CCPA/CPRA service-provider certification stating that Vendor is a “service provider” as defined in Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(ag) and will not sell, share, or retain Customer Data except as necessary to perform the Agreement. The main agreement also references this certification in Sections 6.2 and 6.8.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes GLBA safeguards compliance
criteria_results.reasoning: The DPA expressly addresses GLBA safeguards compliance. Exhibit D, Section 4 states that Customer Data includes NPPI subject to GLBA and requires Vendor to comply with all applicable safeguard requirements. The agreement also references the FTC Safeguards Rule in Section 6.3 and specifies security safeguards in Sections 6.4 and Exhibit D, Section 7.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes 72-hour data breach notification
criteria_results.reasoning: Exhibit D, Section 8 requires Vendor to notify Customer of any confirmed or reasonably suspected Security Breach within seventy-two (72) hours after Vendor first discovers or becomes aware of it.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes sub-processor management with prior written consent
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly requires Customer’s prior written consent before Vendor may engage any sub-processor to process Customer Data, both in Section 6.6 and Section 6 of Exhibit D (the DPA).

criteria_results.title: DPA includes de-identification standards with statutory compliance and independent verification
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 satisfies both requirements. Section 5A of Exhibit D requires de-identified or aggregated data to meet the CCPA statutory standard in Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(m) and requires written verification by an independent third-party assessor approved by Customer before any use. Section 6.1 of the Agreement contains parallel requirements.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes data return/deletion upon termination
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3’s DPA expressly provides in Section 10 that, upon termination or expiration, Vendor must return or delete all Customer Data within 30 days of Customer’s written request and certify the return or deletion in writing.

criteria_results.title: Issues list covers all 12 minimum negotiation point categories
criteria_results.reasoning: The issues list expressly covers all 12 required categories: IP ownership/licensing, liability cap, data processing/de-identification, uptime, latency, accuracy/F1, SLA credits, escrow, AI-output indemnity, IP indemnity scope, Tech E&O insurance, and governing law/dispute resolution.

criteria_results.title: IP ownership/licensing categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes Issue 5, “IP ownership / license structure,” as “Partially Resolved,” reflecting the perpetual-license construct while noting remaining conditions and negotiation points, including portability, non-assertion, escrow, and reserved ownership.

criteria_results.title: Liability cap categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes the liability cap ($3.6M compromise) as "Open," which satisfies the criterion because either "Partially Resolved" or "Open" is acceptable; it is not marked fully resolved.

criteria_results.title: Data processing/de-identification categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: Issue 8, “Data processing / CCPA service-provider,” is expressly categorized as “Partially Resolved.” The issues list notes that service-provider/processor status and a DPA were agreed, while Draft 3 adds the specific de-identification condition, correctly indicating that condition remains TechNova’s proposed treatment rather than a fully resolved term.

criteria_results.title: Uptime SLA categorized as resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes Issue 1, “Uptime SLA (99.95%),” as “Resolved” and states that it applies monthly with the agreed scheduled-maintenance and Force Majeure exclusions, including 72-hour maintenance notice and a four-hour monthly maintenance limit.

criteria_results.title: Latency SLA categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes the latency SLA as “Partially Resolved,” states that Draft 3 accepts Meridian’s p95 ≤ 450 ms offer, and notes that the product team continues to prefer sub-400 ms latency.

criteria_results.title: Accuracy/F1 SLA categorized as open
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes Issue 3, “Accuracy / F1 score,” as Open and states that Draft 3 proposes F1 ≥ 0.92 during stabilization and F1 ≥ 0.94 beginning January 1, 2026, which Meridian has not agreed to.

criteria_results.title: SLA credits categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes SLA credits (Issue 4) as "Open," not fully "Resolved." The criterion expressly accepts either "Partially Resolved" or "Open."

criteria_results.title: Escrow categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes escrow (Issue 13) as “Open,” reflecting that the concept exists but the escrow agent and deposit scope remain disputed. The criterion expressly accepts either “Partially Resolved” or “Open,” so this satisfies it.

criteria_results.title: AI-output indemnity categorized as open
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes Issue 9, “AI-output indemnity,” as “Open” and notes that Meridian had not provided a substantive response.

criteria_results.title: IP indemnity scope categorized as open
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes Issue 10, “IP indemnity scope,” as “Open” and explains that Draft 3 proposes broader coverage that has not yet been agreed by Meridian.

criteria_results.title: Tech E&O insurance categorized as partially resolved with yellow-zone flag
criteria_results.reasoning: Issue 11, “Insurance / Tech E&O ($5M accepted),” is categorized as “Partially Resolved” and expressly flagged “YELLOW ZONE — TCV exceeds $5M.”

criteria_results.title: Governing law/dispute resolution categorized as open
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes item 12, “Governing law / dispute resolution,” as “Open,” noting that Meridian remains at Massachusetts law and AAA arbitration in Boston.

criteria_results.title: Draft 3 is redlined against Draft 2 as the base (not Draft 1)
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 contains tracked insertions and deletions, and the deleted baseline provisions reflect Draft 2 positions—for example, Customer ownership of Customer-Trained Adaptations—while Draft 3 changes those positions through tracked edits. This indicates Draft 2 changes were accepted into the base before the Draft 3 redline was generated.

criteria_results.title: Annual platform fee preserved at $2,400,000/yr
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 preserves the Annual Platform Fee at $2,400,000 per Contract Year in Section 4.1, invoiced as twelve monthly installments of $200,000. The issues list also confirms the same annual fee.

criteria_results.title: 3-year initial term preserved (July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2028)
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 preserves the three-year initial term. The Effective Date is July 1, 2025, and Section 13.1 states that the Initial Term expires on June 30, 2028. The issues list also confirms these dates.

criteria_results.title: Implementation fee preserved at $850,000 with 50/50 milestone split
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 preserves the one-time implementation fee at $850,000, split into two equal $425,000 installments: the first following execution of the Initial SOW and the second following achievement of Go-Live. Exhibit A reflects the same milestone payment schedule.

criteria_results.title: Included API calls preserved at 40,000,000/yr with $0.012 overage
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 preserves 40,000,000 Included API Calls per Contract Year and sets the overage rate at $0.012 per API call in Section 4.3; the issues list also confirms these terms.

criteria_results.title: 180-day auto-renewal notice period preserved
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 13.2 preserves the auto-renewal notice period by requiring either party to provide notice of non-renewal at least 180 days before expiration of the then-current term. The updated issues list also correctly reflects the 180-day notice period.

criteria_results.title: Issues list notes latency 450 ms is within playbook acceptable range but below preferred 400 ms
criteria_results.reasoning: The issues list notes that 450 ms falls short of the product team's preferred sub-400 ms target for LendStream real-time decisioning, but it does not state that 450 ms remains within the playbook's acceptable range of ≤500 ms. The required context is therefore incomplete.

criteria_results.title: Issues list recommends considering latency escalation at the May 19 joint call
criteria_results.reasoning: The latency issue is flagged as product-critical, its fallback recommends revisiting it at the joint call, and latency is expressly listed as a priority for the week-of-May-19 joint call.

criteria_results.title: Issues list flags AI-output indemnity as fully open with no Meridian response
criteria_results.reasoning: The issues list marks “AI-output indemnity” as “Open” and expressly states that Meridian had not provided a substantive response as of the instructions. This satisfies the requirement to identify it as fully open and note Meridian’s lack of substantive response.

criteria_results.title: Issues list notes playbook fallback for AI-output indemnity (shared-risk with vendor first-dollar coverage)
criteria_results.reasoning: The issues list expressly states the fallback for AI-output indemnity: a “shared-risk framework with Meridian first-dollar coverage for defense, settlements, and judgments up to the applicable cap / super-cap.” This satisfies the criterion.
